newsitem.title: UK: OPEC JULY CRUDE OUTPUT UP 170K BPD TO 26.5 MLN-IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC JULY CRUDE OUTPUT UP 170K BPD TO 26.5 MLN-IEA.

text.p: Production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose by 170,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.5 million bpd in July due mostly to output hikes from middle eastern member countries, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

With the continued absence of Iraqi exports OPEC crude supply only marginally exceeded the downwardly revised figure of 26.33 million bpd for June, the IEA said in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report.
Estimates derived from tanker tracking data point to a gain in Iranian production of 75,000 bpd and there are indications that production in Saudi Arabia rose by 25,000 bpd, the IEA said.
Kuwaiti supply rose marginally by 10,000 bpd offsetting a similar drop from the United Arab Emirates.
Output in Qatar rose 5,000 bpd to 620,000 bpd while Iraqi production held unchanged at 550,000 bpd.

Producers outside the Middle East increased production by 23,000 bpd with most of the rise coming from Venezuela where production averaged 3.19 million bpd in July. Changes in other countries offset each other.

There was a drop in Nigerian output of 20,000 bpd as delays in payments by the Nigerian state oil company to joint venture partners resulted in some deferrals or slowdowns in routine development work.
There were slight gains in Algerian production of 10,000 bpd and in Indonesia where supply rose 15,000 bpd.
Libyan supply dropped slightly to 1.43 million bpd in July.
